parsed.explanation: Thin-data but structurally favourable: same-sex conduct legal since 1869, no trans-specific criminal offence, no facility/entry restrictions, no police targeting or sweeps documented, and LGBTI organisations can register and litigate successfully (2017/2022 gender-marker rulings, though unexecuted). No universal-exposure measure is recorded; unknowns (custody placement, border practice) are open questions, not exposures, per rubric rule 13. Weighing against this: documented 'daily discrimination, violence and stigmatisation' against LGBTI people broadly (2024 UN submission), discrimination noted by a 2015 foreign report, exclusion of advocacy groups from consultation, and no hate-crime statute shown to cover gender identity. Absence of legal gender recognition is a resident gap, not visitor exposure. No documented acceptance tradition offsets the discrimination record, but nothing supports severity beyond tier-3 social friction with partial recourse. Extrapolating from non-criminalisation plus partial protective machinery plus documented societal discrimination: mid-reduced risk, above the 0.45/0.55 band's unremedied exposures, below 0.75 for thin recourse and no evidence of trans-specific acceptance.
